en: Vimānavatthu:
The Chapter on the Pāricchattaka Tree in the Itthivimāna (The Female Vimānas)
4. The Story of the Latā Mansion The goddesses Latā, Sajjā, Pavarā,
and Accimatī [attended] upon the illustrious and noble King Sirīmat.
And Suta, the daughter of King Vessavaṇa,
and Rājīmatī shone with the qualities of the Dhamma.
Five women came there to bathe.
Having bathed there in that auspicious river of cool water and lotuses,
and having delighted themselves by dancing and singing,
those deities spoke to the creeper they had heard.
“I ask you, O wearer of lotus garlands,
with braided hair and skin like refined gold;
with eyes as dark-brown as a bee, you shine like the sky.”
By what means was long life secured? By what was your fame made?
By what, O Bhaddā, have you become dearer than your husband, being more distinguished and more beautiful in form than others?
“You have been asked by men and women about the right course regarding dancing, singing, and instrumental music; please explain it to us.
“I was born among humans as a human being...”
I was a daughter-in-law in a family of abundant wealth;
free from anger, I followed the will of my husband,
and I was diligent in observing the Uposatha.
Having been born as humans, young and blameless,
with a clear mind, I pleased my husband;
together with his deities, his parents-in-law, and his kinsmen.
I performed acts of honor for him there,
and through that wholesome deed,
I attained distinction in four respects.
“Longevity, beauty, happiness, and strength,
And the experience of abundant play and delight.
“Does this creeper speak what it has heard?”
What we asked, he has explained to us:
"He is indeed our husband, the most distinguished among women;
his destination is supreme, and he is a preeminent deity."
Let us all practice the duty toward husbands in which women are devoted;
having practiced the duty toward husbands, all of us—
"O Lakṣmī, this creeper speaks what she says.
Like a lion whose range is the mountain ridges,
having taken up residence on Mount Mahindhara,"
Having attacked and slain other four-footed creatures,
he eats their flesh, subsisting on meat.
In the same way, the noble female disciple here possesses faith;
Devoted to her husband and relying on him as her lord,
having slain anger and overcome stinginess,
that woman who walks in the Dhamma rejoices in heaven.
The fourth is the Latāvimāna.
